case2_style_sign_reversal.note: Sign convention: d = gamma_TV - gamma_VT (the stored archive reports mean_difference = gamma_VT - gamma_TV = -0.0219 for the DS-exec/Qwen-eval archive, i.e., the same magnitude with the opposite sign). For both 30-repetition archives, the sign of d is highly unstable when estimated from 5-seed subsamples: 49.6% of DS-exec/Qwen-eval 5-subsets and 84.3% of DS-self-eval 5-subsets produce a sign opposite to the full-sample estimate. This quantifies the N-sensitivity of Case-2-type comparisons and supports reporting reversal probability and CI overlap rather than point estimates.

cv_ranking_stability_simulation.note: In the 200-seed simulation, gamma rankings are monotone in alpha and CV rankings are perfectly stable between N=5 and N=30 (Spearman/Kendall = 1.0). The simulation therefore does NOT exhibit rank reversal; the N-sensitivity signature appears as a systematic CV magnitude decrease with N, not as a ranking flip. Rank instability is instead observed in the real-data Case-2-style subsample analysis above, which is where reversal probability matters.

decision_rule_draft.class: B (method/definition addition, no new data required)
decision_rule_draft.rule: Declare N-sensitivity for a comparison of quantities q_N vs q_{N'} (N' > N) when ALL of the following hold: (1) [Reversal] the sign or rank order of the estimated comparison differs between N and N' under fixed analysis code, seeds, and aggregation; (2) [Magnitude] |q_N - q_{N'}| exceeds a predeclared equivalence margin m (e.g., m = 0.10 in standardized units), not merely statistical significance; (3) [Replication] the reversal reproduces in at least a predeclared fraction (e.g., 80%) of bootstrap or seed-subsample replications of size N drawn from the available seed pool; (4) [Scope] the reversal is not attributable to a change in target quantity, estimator, or exclusion rule between N and N' (checked by frozen code and a change log). If (1)-(3) hold but (4) is violated, the comparison is not N-sensitive but design-sensitive.
